questions.prompt: A person who designs and builds useful machines by applying scientific knowledge is called a:
questions.explanation: A technologist is a person who studies and makes technology, using scientific knowledge to build useful machines and solutions.

questions.prompt: Which laboratory tool is used to give a flame for heating substances?
questions.explanation: A Bunsen burner produces a flame and is used for heating substances in the laboratory.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: The jelly-like fluid inside a cell where the cell parts float and many reactions happen is the:
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid that fills the cell, holds the cell parts, and is where many chemical reactions take place.

questions.prompt: In the memory word MRS GREN, the letter G stands for which characteristic of living things?
questions.explanation: In MRS GREN, G stands for Growth, the ability of living things to become bigger and more complex over time.

questions.prompt: The thin outer layer of the Earth, made of solid rock, on which we live is called the:
questions.explanation: The crust is the thin, solid, rocky outer layer of the Earth where the land and oceans are found.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: Energy that is stored in an object because of its raised position, such as a rock at the top of a hill, is called:
questions.explanation: Potential energy is stored energy that depends on an object's position, such as a rock held high on a hill.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: A push or a pull that can change the motion or shape of an object is called a:
questions.explanation: A force is a push or a pull that can start, stop, speed up, slow down, or change the shape of an object.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a physical change?
questions.explanation: Cutting paper only changes its form; no new substance is made, so it is a physical change. The others form new substances.

questions.prompt: The field that combines physics and chemistry to study how energy affects substances is called:
questions.explanation: Physical chemistry combines physics and chemistry to study the physical behaviour of substances and how energy affects them.

questions.prompt: Which value shows good scientific ethics when a scientist reports results exactly as they were observed, even if surprising?
questions.explanation: Honesty is a key scientific ethic; a scientist must report results truthfully and exactly as observed.

questions.prompt: When water vapour in the air cools and turns back into liquid water droplets, the change is called:
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change from a gas (water vapour) back to a liquid when it cools, forming droplets.

questions.prompt: A mixture of oil and water is left to settle, then the top oil is carefully poured off, leaving the water behind. This method is called:
questions.explanation: Decantation separates substances by pouring off the upper layer of liquid after the heavier part has settled or separated.

questions.prompt: Which property is typical of a metal element?
options: It is dull and does not conduct electricity
It is shiny and conducts electricity
questions.explanation: Metals such as iron, copper, and gold are shiny and conduct electricity, unlike most non-metals.

questions.prompt: In the formula CaCO₃, the small number 3 written below and to the right of O is called a:
questions.explanation: The small number written below and to the right in a formula is a subscript; it tells how many atoms of that element are present.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: When carrying a microscope from one table to another, you should hold it by the:
questions.explanation: A microscope must be carried by holding the arm and supporting the base, to keep it safe and steady.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: Which part of a microscope controls how much light passes through the specimen?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm controls the amount of light that passes up through the specimen, making the image easier to see.

questions.prompt: Which kingdom contains tiny, single-celled organisms such as bacteria that do NOT have a true nucleus?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera contains very small single-celled organisms such as bacteria that lack a true (membrane-bound) nucleus.

questions.prompt: A mango tree makes its own food using sunlight. Based on this, it belongs to which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis and belong to Kingdom Plantae.

questions.prompt: All the rocks and soil that form the solid land of the Earth make up which part of the Earth system?
questions.explanation: The lithosphere is the solid part of the Earth, made of rocks and soil, including the crust and upper mantle.

questions.prompt: Which movement of the Earth is responsible for the changing seasons during the year?
options: Revolution around the Sun with a tilted axis
questions.explanation: The Earth's revolution around the Sun, together with its tilted axis, causes different parts to receive more or less sunlight, giving seasons.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: A car wheel turning around its centre while the car stays in one spot shows which type of motion?
questions.explanation: Rotational motion is movement around a fixed centre or axis, such as a wheel spinning in place.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Sunlight is renewable because it is naturally replaced and will not run out, unlike coal, oil, and natural gas.

questions.prompt: A bowl contains a mixture of dry beans and rice that you can clearly see as separate grains. This is best described as a:
questions.explanation: A heterogeneous mixture has parts you can see separately, like beans and rice mixed together but still visible as different grains.

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are present in one unit of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆?
questions.explanation: Glucose has 6 carbon, 12 hydrogen, and 6 oxygen atoms, giving a total of 6 + 12 + 6 = 24 atoms.

questions.prompt: Which is the correctly balanced equation for the burning of methane, CH₄, in oxygen?
questions.explanation: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O has 1 carbon, 4 hydrogen, and 4 oxygen atoms on each side, so it is balanced.

questions.prompt: A sealed bottle is half full of water. The water slowly disappears from the bottom and tiny drops appear on the upper inside walls. Which two changes are happening together?
questions.explanation: The liquid water evaporates into vapour and then condenses back into droplets on the cooler upper walls of the bottle.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: A microscope has an eyepiece of 10× and three objective lenses of 4×, 10×, and 40×. What is the highest total magnification it can give?
questions.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective. The highest is 10 × 40 = 400 times.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares the cell membrane and the cell wall?
options: Both are found only in animal cells
The membrane is in all cells, but the wall is only in plant cells
The wall is in all cells, but the membrane is only in plant cells
Neither controls what enters the cell
questions.explanation: Every cell has a cell membrane that controls what enters and leaves, but only plant cells have the extra rigid cell wall.

questions.prompt: A mushroom cannot make its own food and instead absorbs nutrients from dead matter. Which kingdom does it belong to?
questions.explanation: Mushrooms are fungi; they cannot make their own food and absorb nutrients from dead or living matter, so they belong to Kingdom Fungi.

questions.prompt: During a clear night, the stars appear to move slowly across the sky from east to west. What actually causes this apparent movement?
options: The Earth rotating on its axis
questions.explanation: The Earth's rotation on its axis makes the sky, including the stars, appear to move from east to west, although it is really the Earth turning.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: A boy rubs his cold hands together quickly and they become warm. The main energy change is from:
questions.explanation: The movement of the hands (kinetic energy) is changed by friction into heat energy, which warms the hands.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up into the air. At its highest point, just before it starts to fall, what has happened to its energy?
options: All of it is still kinetic energy
It has gained new chemical energy
Most of its kinetic energy has changed into potential energy
questions.explanation: As the ball rises it slows down, so its kinetic energy is changed into potential energy, which is greatest at the highest point.

questions.prompt: A scientist observes a problem, asks a question, forms a testable guess, and then does an experiment to check it. The testable guess in this process is the:
questions.explanation: In the scientific method, the testable guess made before experimenting is the hypothesis, which the experiment is designed to test.

questions.prompt: In a closed jar, 10 g of a substance reacts completely and forms a gas and a solid. According to the law of conservation of mass, the total mass of the gas and solid together is:
questions.explanation: By the law of conservation of mass, matter is not created or destroyed, so the products must have the same total mass as the reactants, 10 g.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: Two cells are compared. Cell X has a nucleus, mitochondria, a cell wall, and chloroplasts. Cell Y has a nucleus and mitochondria but no cell wall and no chloroplasts. Which is true?
options: X is an animal cell and Y is a plant cell
X is a plant cell and Y is an animal cell
questions.explanation: A cell with a cell wall and chloroplasts (X) is a plant cell, while a cell with neither (Y) is an animal cell.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: A solar panel on a roof powers an electric lamp at night using a battery charged during the day. Trace the main energy changes in the correct order.
questions.explanation: Sunlight (light energy) becomes electrical energy in the panel, is stored as chemical energy in the battery, then becomes electrical energy again, and finally light energy in the lamp.
